bullets.title: June CPI Shock: Headline -0.4% MoM, Core 0.0% — Biggest Monthly Drop Since COVID
bullets.body: June headline CPI fell 0.4% MoM (vs. -0.1% est.) and 3.5% YoY (vs. 3.8% est., prior 4.2%); core CPI came in flat at 0.0% MoM (vs. +0.2% est.) and 2.6% YoY (vs. 2.8% est.). Supercore services fell 0.2% MoM — the largest drop since pandemic lockdowns — while shelter rose just 0.1% MoM, the smallest gain since January 2021. 3-month annualized CPI collapsed from 8.2% to 2.8%, and one-year inflation swaps dropped below 2% for the first time since 2024.

bullets.title: Rate-Hike Odds Plunge to 13-14% Post-CPI; Short-End Yields Drop 10bps
bullets.body: Following the CPI beat, traders sharply cut Fed rate-hike bets for this month, with futures pricing hike odds at just 13-14%. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 10bps. September hike odds now show a 12% arbitrage spread between Polymarket (~40%) and SOFR futures (~52%), a whipsaw from 60% odds just Monday after Waller's hawkish remarks.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh: 'Mission Accomplished' Not My View — Inflation Remains a Policy Choice
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh in Congressional testimony rejected the 'mission accomplished' narrative on inflation despite the cool CPI print, characterizing inflation as a deliberate policy choice and pledging the Fed has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.' He cautioned against overreacting to a single data point, wants multiple months of PCE-CPI consistency before gaining confidence, and flagged that high 30-year mortgage rates stem from inflation above the Fed's target. UBS noted Warsh struck a 'resolutely hawkish tone.'

bullets.title: Warsh on Fed Independence, Regime Change, and Balance Sheet Tools
bullets.body: Warsh pledged Fed independence from political pressure, committed to data-driven policy even if Trump criticizes him, and announced broad reforms across supervision, regulation, and payments systems. He characterized the 2020 Fed framework as 'a mistake' and signaled a 'sea change in new thinking' over just six weeks. He also clarified that dollar swap lines are monetary policy tools and that Treasury can deploy the ESF for swap lines independently of the Fed.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Escalation: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain; Hormuz Open Except for Iranian Ships
bullets.body: Iran fired missiles and drones at Kuwait and Bahrain, and Qeshm/Kish Island explosions were reported. Trump responded by declaring the Strait of Hormuz open to all ship traffic except Iran, announced a full blockade on Iranian shipping, and scrapped the proposed 20% cargo transit fee in favor of trade/investment deals from Gulf states. Oil futures briefly went negative before settling near $78-79/bbl WTI as de-escalation signals offset the military strikes.

bullets.title: Nvidia H200 Shipments to China Have Begun; Volume Described as 'Trivial'
bullets.body: A senior U.S. official confirmed that a small initial batch of NVDA H200 chips has cleared licensing, inspection, and customs to be delivered to China and Hong Kong — the first such shipments occurring roughly two months after the Trump-Xi meeting. Commerce official Kessler characterized the volume as 'trivial,' and analysts cautioned that large-scale H200 shipments have not resumed; it appears only ~10 previously licensed Chinese entities received chips.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Partners with Mitsubishi Heavy on AI Data Center Cooling and Power
bullets.body: Per Nikkei, NVIDIA is eyeing a cooperation agreement with Mitsubishi Heavy on AI data center cooling infrastructure and power solutions, extending NVDA's ecosystem play beyond chips into facility-level infrastructure.

bullets.title: NY State Imposes First U.S. Statewide Data Center Moratorium — One-Year Ban
bullets.body: New York became the first state to enact a statewide one-year moratorium on new data center construction, citing energy price and environmental concerns. The ban was enacted via executive order (not law), and JMP Citizens noted it can be reversed once cost-benefit clarity improves. Market consensus: US scale is large enough that even 25+ state moratoriums would not materially constrain capacity, and tax incentives suggest ample alternative build locations.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector: SOX -5% Yesterday Then +5% Pre-Market; MU Whale Prints $6.5M Overnight
bullets.body: The SOX ETF (SOXX) swung nearly 10% over two sessions, averaging +/-3.36% daily moves over the last 50 days. A whale accumulated $16.3M in short-dated MU calls and netted $6.5M overnight as Micron gapped up on the CPI print. Lower inflation and rate expectations described as broadly bullish for the memory/storage and AI infrastructure trade.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Trade Shifting: 2023-25 Infrastructure Phase → 2026 Model-Lab Phase
bullets.body: Analysts note the 2023-2025 trade centered on infrastructure (TSMC, Nvidia, Vistra, GE Vernova, memory) is giving way to a 2026 model-lab trade as Anthropic ARR surged from ~$9B end-2024 to $44B+ YTD. Goldman Sachs hit an all-time high, framed as a diversified AI capex cycle financial intermediary across M&A, equity/debt issuance, and data center/power financing.

bullets.title: Citadel Securities: Market No Longer Driven by Positioning — Back to Fundamentals
bullets.body: Citadel Securities' chief strategist declared the market has shifted from a positioning-driven regime to a fundamentals-driven one, while simultaneously warning of a potential 'three bears' scenario — questioning whether the Goldilocks era is over.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Breadth Narrowing: Top 10 Names Now 43% of Market Cap; Average Stock -33bps
bullets.body: The ten largest S&P 500 firms represent 43% of total market cap. On today's session the average S&P 500 stock was down 33bps, with Health Care and Consumer sectors leading declines. A long-run study shows only 27.6% of stocks outperform the market while 60% destroy shareholder wealth, underscoring the concentration dynamic.

bullets.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism Beats at 97.4 vs. 95.7 Estimate
bullets.body: NFIB Small Business Optimism rose to 97.4 in June, beating the 95.7 consensus estimate. Inflation remains the single most important problem cited by small businesses, followed by taxes and labor quality. The Misery Index (CPI YoY + unemployment) declined to 7.7% from 8.5% in May, driven by pullback in energy prices.

bullets.title: Bank Earnings Broadly Strong: JPMorgan Best Quarter Ever; Goldman at All-Time High
bullets.body: JPMorgan posted its best quarter ever by revenue; CEO Dimon described the U.S. economy as demonstrating 'notable resiliency' with stronger business investment and hiring. Goldman Sachs shares hit an all-time high driven by robust M&A pipeline and AI capex cycle intermediation. JPMorgan sold $4.6B of Visa stock in Q2 held since its 2008 IPO. Citigroup Q2 revenue beat at $24.77B vs. $23.74B est., with equities trading revenue of $2.3B vs. $1.9B est.

bullets.title: UBER in Advanced Talks to Acquire Delivery Hero for ~$13B at Significant Premium
bullets.body: Uber is in advanced talks to acquire German food-delivery company Delivery Hero, planning to bid well above the recent market price; Delivery Hero is valued at just under $13B. UBER shares initially declined ~2.5% on the news.

bullets.title: Apple Down 1.1% Pre-Market on KeyBanc Underweight Downgrade; In Talks With PrismML for On-Device AI
bullets.body: KeyBanc cut AAPL to underweight from sector weight, citing weaker device demand and slower US service revenue growth. Separately, Apple is in talks with PrismML, a startup that compresses AI models to run natively on iPhones — potentially reducing reliance on cloud inference. Apple also faces a lawsuit from OpenAI (per Stratechery).

bullets.title: China Scaling Domestic DRAM and GPU Production; Chipmakers JHICC, YMTC, CXMT Expanding
bullets.body: China is scaling up domestic DRAM and GPU manufacturing capacity in response to expanding U.S. export controls. CXMT priced its Shanghai IPO at 8.66 yuan/share. Yuliangsheng's DUV immersion lithography expected in mass production by 2028, with JHICC and YMTC also expected to expand rapidly post-2028 — structural long-run headwind for U.S. memory and chip suppliers' China TAM.

bullets.title: Enterprise SaaS Soft on IBM Contagion: HUBS Tracking 10-15% Below Plan per Rayjay
bullets.body: IBM's 25%+ collapse on a software revenue warning is weighing on enterprise SaaS sentiment broadly. Raymond James reportedly flagged HubSpot as tracking 10-15% below plan, and WDAY, TEAM, NOW also cited as facing rough sessions on IBM pre-announcement contagion. IBM's miss was driven by Software & Infrastructure underperformance with Q2 revenue of $17.2B vs. $17.9B est.

bullets.title: AI Productivity Narrative Questioned: Q2 Data Shows No Macro Takeoff
bullets.body: Multiple commentators pushed back on 'greatest invention in human history' AI productivity claims — macro data shows no quarterly productivity takeoff, with Q2 expected to show similar dynamics. Global bond markets are under pressure from exploding debt issuance, and AI's actual impact on GDP remains well below hype, per observer analysis.

bullets.title: GOOGL Signs 1.6GW Arkansas Solar PPA — Largest Solar Project of Its Kind in U.S.
bullets.body: Google agreed to purchase 100% of the energy output from the Steel River Energy Center, a 1.6GW solar project in Arkansas expected to begin operations in 2029, described as the biggest solar project of its kind to break ground in the U.S.
